summary: Two eligible contexts: the CERAMINOL wine-lees ceramide RCT (38999848; 29 adults with dry skin, 100 mg/day for 12 weeks) lowered the primary TEWL versus placebo at 12 weeks (p=0.04) with null secondary outcomes, and the ceramide subgroup of a 66-RCT meta-analysis (35719159) showed improved skin hydration (SMD 0.40, 7 studies) and TEWL (7 trials) for single-preparation ceramides at 0.4-30 mg/day. The open-label rice-ceramide study (35807914) is approved without credit. 33055441 (acetic acid bacteria, 0.8 mg dihydroceramide) is abstract-only and gets no context.

applicability.studied_population: Healthy adults, including adults with self-reported dry skin, taking oral ceramide supplements (0.4-30 mg/day ceramides) for 6-20 weeks.

identity.standardization: Wine lees extract with cyclodextrin; 100 mg/day provides >=2 mg ceramides and glucosylceramides (HPLC)

population.description: 30 healthy Japanese adults aged 20-64 with self-reported dry skin, stratified by sex, age and baseline TEWL; 29 analysed (test 14, placebo 15).

study_contexts.study_design: Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled parallel trial, 12 weeks (UMIN000050422).

outcomes.name: Primary TEWL (forearm): significantly lower than placebo at 12 weeks (p=0.04); trend at 8 weeks (p=0.07)
Skin hydration, itching VAS and Skindex-29: no significant between-group differences

limitations: Small trial (29 analysed); only the 12-week primary timepoint was significant; secondary hydration and symptom outcomes null.
Exact wine-lees ceramide material; no equivalence to wheat, rice, konjac or bacterial ceramides or to a total-mass threshold.

population.description: Ceramide subset of a 66-RCT review: 11 studies (601 participants) in healthy adults over 6-20 weeks; 7 single-preparation studies (426) pooled for hydration and 7 for TEWL.

study_contexts.study_design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs of oral skin supplements (PROSPERO CRD42021290818); ingredient-specific ceramide subgroup, single versus combination preparations analysed separately.

outcomes.name: Stratum corneum water content, single-preparation ceramides vs placebo: SMD 0.40 (95% CI 0.04-0.76), p=0.03, 7 studies, n=426
TEWL, single-preparation ceramides: effect -0.29 (95% CI -0.49 to -0.10), p=0.003, 7 trials
Combination preparations with ceramides (2 studies, n=53): hydration SMD 0.63 (-0.67 to 1.94), p=0.34

limitations: Different ceramide sources pooled; no wheat/rice/bacterial equivalence. Doses 0.4-30 mg/day ceramides in eight studies; no threshold.
